public_rationale: GitHub announced that all Copilot plans billed by AI Credits consumed from June 1, 2026; this establishes a change within one product family [e1]. The October 22 preprint reports usage-quota subscriptions in 55% of observable AI-native rows, while 23 of 52 AI-native rows publish no pricing [e2]. Its quota category and selected cohorts do not establish a representative majority moving specifically to token-based billing [e2]. Neither item establishes the claimed market-wide transition or makes its eventual occurrence impossible [e1, e2].
limitations: No representative denominator for AI subscription products is established.
Usage quotas alone do not establish token-based billing.
The study does not count how many products changed to token-based billing.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The majority of AI subscriptions will inevitably move to token-based billing.

statement.excerpt: I think it’s inevitable that the majority of AI subscriptions move to token-based billing, especially as both Anthropic and OpenAI have now done so with their enterprise customers.

our_interpretation: Majority means more than half. I read subscriptions as subscription products, rather than weighting products by subscribers or revenue.
Token-based billing includes credits whose consumption depends on token use. A request limit or generic usage quota alone does not establish token-based billing.
The claim requires a market-wide transition. Examples from several prominent providers cannot establish the denominator.
criteria.support_condition: Dated, sufficiently representative evidence establishes that more than half of AI subscription products have moved to billing tied to token consumption.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive event makes the claimed eventual majority transition impossible. Continued availability of flat-rate plans at an interim date does not contradict an undated forecast.
